firstWrongStep: After integrating by parts you wrote $\int_0^{\pi} \sin x \, dx = \big[ \cos x \big]_0^{\pi}$.
feedback: Your set-up is correct: $u = x$ and $dv = \cos x \, dx$ are the right choices, and the boundary term $\big[ x \sin x \big]_0^{\pi}$ is evaluated correctly. The first error is in the next line: an antiderivative of $\sin x$ is $-\cos x$, not $\cos x$. Because of the missing minus sign, the sign of the second term is wrong and it carries through to your final line. Redo the integral of $\sin x$ from that line onwards.
overallFeedback: Good method and a clear layout; one sign slip in a standard integral cost you the final answer. Check standard antiderivatives by differentiating them.
